events.title: I Am Human: Storytime + Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Calling All Humans! Join author-illustrator Laura G. Lee for a special I Am Human book launch, storytime, and creative workshop. Laura will begin with a reading of I Am Human and a playful conversation inspired by the book: What does it mean to be human? How are we different from AI—and how do we know? After the reading, participants are invited to join a hands-on writing and drawing workshop, responding to creative prompts through words and pictures, enjoying snacks, and sharing ideas. All ages are welcome. The workshop is especially well suited to older elementary kids, teens, and adults, while younger children are welcome to enjoy the story time portion with their families. Workshop RSVPs are encouraged so we can prepare enough materials.
events.blurb: Hear Laura G. Lee read I Am Human, then join a playful conversation about what it means to be human.

events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Storytime with Claire Wrenn Bobrow
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Claire Wrenn Bobrow returns to Linden Tree to share her delightful new picture book, Party Pony! Not another party! Parties used to be Pony's favorite—until every bash turned him into a work horse! Now Pony is a party pooper. How will Pony's friends show him he's worthy of a party too? For any kid who's ever felt left out, this witty picture book is a must-have for the home or school library, and it's perfect for gifting and reading at parties. Grab your copy and join the celebration!
events.blurb: Hear author Claire Wrenn Bobrow read her new picture book, Party Pony!, about a pony who has grown tired of parties.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Home Scientist (Brownies)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Science is all around us! Brownies begin by making pepper dance using the amazing properties of electricity. Next, they become kitchen chemists and use pantry items to make art with delicious treats. Then they explore properties of density and use them to blow up a balloon without breath and make their own lava lamp. Finally, Brownies will learn how science can be used to make toys and make their very own silly putty! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Home Scientist Badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Make pepper dance with electricity, then use pantry items as a kitchen chemist in this Brownies Home Scientist program.

events.title: Storytime with Sahar Shams
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Sahar Shams shares her festive debut picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas? Every year, children all around the world ask themselves what they'd like to receive from Santa. But one little boy has a different question: What would Santa wish for? Determined, Dorim sets out on a quest to craft the perfect present—but he'll need some help from his friends. With Christmas fast approaching, will they be able to make Santa's wish come true in time?
events.blurb: Hear debut author Sahar Shams read her festive picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas?, at a Sunday storytime.

events.title: Drop-in Teens Reach Volunteering
events.description: Perfect for young teens just starting out their volunteering journey - come to Rose Garden to get some in-person volunteering experience! Teens of all ages are welcome to join our Drop-In Volunteer Hour every second Friday afternoon from 4 PM-5 PM to help with a variety of library tasks, such as creating and building book displays, tidying up spaces, decorating for holidays, maintaining craft materials and supplies, etc. No previous experience is needed, just a desire to help! Signing up for Teens Reach is encouraged, although not required. This event is a Volunteer Away Your Fines event. This is a free event; no prior registration is required. A parent signature is required to participate in this program. Please reach out to jeff.brenion@sjlibrary.org for a PDF copy of the form that can be printed and signed prior to participating.
events.blurb: Drop in to help with library tasks and log volunteer hours with fellow teens.

events.title: Almaden Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Join our teen service group and earn community service credit, supporting the community by assisting with book displays, presenting children's programs, running book sales and more. Learn about teen volunteer opportunities by attending our monthly meetings - every second Friday of each month. Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. If you are new to volunteering with San Jose Public Library, please check out Teens Reach: Community Service for more information. If you wish to apply, click "Sign Me Up" under Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Meet with the teen service group to plan book displays, book sales, and children's programs for credit.

events.title: STEM: Archimedes Screw Model
events.description: Screws are one of the simple machines that we use every day: they are used as hardware for building, but additionally, bottle caps, doorknobs, and standard light bulbs are also examples of screws. In this activity, patrons will create models of screws with different distances (pitch) between the inclined planes or ramps (threads) to find out which one will move a marble across a certain distance with fewer turns. The program is recommended for patrons ages 8-12. No registration required; first-come, first-served; capacity is limited. events.title: The 10 Laws of Finance for Business Owners
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Join us for an exclusive, two-hour in-person workshop designed to transform how you view and manage your company's financial health: Ten decisions every business leader needs to understand, measure, and improve. Through real-world benchmarks and practical frameworks, this workshop exposes the hidden variables that separate fragile revenue from sustainable wealth. You will walk away with an actionable blueprint to test your growth stories against reality, identify single points of failure, and accurately price risk before taking on major commitments. Key topics by law: 1. You Cannot Fix What You Hide - Clean financial inventory: cash, debt, margins, obligations, owner pay, and what the business can actually afford. 2. Displaying Wealth Consumes It - Separate spending that creates strength from spending that signals success: office, vehicles, tools, branding, lifestyle, and unnecessary fixed costs. 3. A Number Alone Will Lie to You - Interpret revenue, growth, headcount, profit, followers, and cash through context: trend, benchmark, margin, risk, and alternative use of capital. 4. Accuracy Emerges from Error - Build a monthly forecast, compare actuals to expectations, and use the variance to improve decisions instead of avoiding uncertainty. 5. Present Decisions Create Exponential Future Impact - Recurring pricing, margin, debt, hiring, churn, customer-quality, and reinvestment decisions compound through the business. 6. Potential Is a Story; Cash Flow Is Reality - Test every growth story against cash timing, working capital, debt service, owner stress, and operating capacity. 7. The Only Worthwhile Risks Command Incremental Expected Rewards - Price major risks before leases, loans, hiring, inventory, product launches, or expansion. Upside must be incremental and downside must be survivable. 8. Concentration Creates Unnecessary Fragility - Identify single points of failure: one customer, one supplier, one platform, one lender, one employee, one owner, or one source of demand. 9. Every Yes Has a Casualty - Use opportunity cost and a hurdle rate before adding customers, products, obligations, marketing channels, hires, or commitments. 10. Success Hardens into Constraints - Review whether old systems, founder habits, informal approvals, legacy pricing, and identity-based decisions are now limiting the next stage. Additional Resources: Free courses, calculators, templates, guides, and practice materials are available at the course. Free. No registration required. Presented by Silicon Valley Small Business Development Center. Silicon Valley SBDC is part of a 40-year national legacy committed to small business success. With unparalleled access to no-cost expertise from entrepreneurs who have seen it all, Silicon Valley SBDC at San Jose State University provides small businesses with the solutions they seek and the confidence they need to realize their dreams. Parking validation for the garage at 88 S. 4th Street will be provided at the program. E-newsletter Signup: Get the inside scoop on business and career resources at SJPL. Sign up today for our monthly e-newsletter, highlighting the latest programs, e-resources and services available at the San José Public Library. #sjplworksbusiness

events.title: Saturday STEM: Bending Light!
events.description: Join our volunteer Kimmie for a study in the physics of light, specifically, how light bends when it passes through different materials. If we trap light within a material, we call this Total Internal Reflection. Kids will see and experience various demonstrations of this effect, then have a chance to build a small fiber optic light toy to play with during the program. This program is appropriate for kids in 2nd grade and up. Space is limited to 15 participants on a first-come, first-served basis. Tickets will be available at the Front Desk one hour before the event begins to secure a spot.

events.title: Master Gardeners: The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces
events.description: Join a Santa Clara County Master Gardener for a monthly talk on various topics. This month: Are you experiencing the "holiday guest stress syndrome"? Don't let the pressure of having a perfect tablescape wilt your holiday spirit! Join UC Master Gardeners Laura Westley and Bernie Day for an inspiring, hands-on demonstration designed to take the stress—and the high cost—out of holiday decorating. You don't need a professional florist or a massive budget to create a "wow" factor for your dining room. What You'll Learn: The Art of the "Found" Object: Learn how to scout your own backyard or junk drawer for unique textures, greenery, and accents that add character to any arrangement. Grocery Store Glam: Discover how to deconstruct those affordable supermarket flower bunches and reimagine them into high-end-looking centerpieces. Pro-Tips for Longevity: Get the inside scoop on keeping your flora fresh from the first toast to the final slice of pie. Why join us? Whether you're hosting a grand feast or an intimate gathering, you'll walk away with the confidence and practical skills to transform "ordinary" items into extraordinary focal points. Upcoming topics are: November 14 - The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces. No talk in December. Detailed program descriptions to be updated when available. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Hear a Santa Clara County Master Gardener talk about creating holiday centerpieces and tablescapes that ease the stress of hosting guests.

events.title: Documentaries: Holodomor Remembrance Day
events.description: The Holodomor, the famine that killed millions of Ukrainians in the 1930s, was not widely known or acknowledged until the fall of the Soviet Union in the 1990s. Established in 1998, Holodomor Remembrance Day is observed on the fourth Saturday of November to remember those who died during the Holodomor. Join us for Palo Alto City Library's second annual program commemorating this event and its lasting effects for some in our community today. Three short documentaries will give us the historical background that reverberates in current events. Descriptions of the documentaries below were written by their creators. Holodomor: How Millions of Ukrainians Died of Starvation During Stalin-Era Mass Famine (Radio Free Europe, 2019, two minutes). Each year, on the fourth Saturday of November, Ukraine remembers the millions who died during the Holodomor, the Stalin-era famine that devastated the population in 1932-1933. Many countries consider it to have been genocide. Minnesota Memories of the Holodomor (PBS, 2025, 26 minutes). In an extraordinary exploration of the transmission of traumatic memory within families, communities and across generations, Ukrainians in Minneapolis-St. Paul share their family stories about the Holodomor artificial famine of 1932-33 and the local community's efforts to come to terms with genocide, even as war once again threatens the existence of Ukrainians as a people. Holodomor: Voices of Survivors (2015, 30 minutes). Twenty-five Ukrainian Canadians tell their stories of survival during the Holodomor--death inflicted by starvation--a genocide of Ukrainian people engineered by Joseph Stalin during 1932 and 1933. Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continue to reverberate today. Books on this reading list will be on display and available. Registration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Everyone Can Create: Beginning Stop Motion Animation
events.description: Children ages 6-12 are invited to this fun, in-person introduction to stop motion animation. Participants will use the Stop Motion Studio app to make simple stop motion animations using small toys and paper. Participants will have an opportunity to showcase their work at the end of the session. iPad devices will be provided to all participants. The theme of all five classes in November is Thanksgiving/Fall. November 1: Introduction to Stop-Motion Animation. Children will learn how stop-motion animation works and create their own Thanksgiving/Autumn props and characters for their movie. November 8: Creating the Halloween Story. Children will develop their Thanksgiving story and begin planning the scenes, characters, and settings for their movie. November 15 and 22: Filming the Movie. Children will use their characters and props to film their Thanksgiving movie, learning how to move objects and characters frame by frame. November 29: Finishing the Movie. Children will complete their animation, add final details, and watch their Thanksgiving movies come to life! Free. Registration required.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to live the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees? Excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each. How do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.attendanceNote: Registration is not required. Optional signup provides a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Learn from UC Master Gardeners how to plan and plant a small fruit orchard, from choosing among plums, apricots, peaches and apples.

events.title: Medicare: Enrollment, 2027 Updates and Plan Review Tips
events.description: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) runs from October 15 through December 7 each year. During this time, Medicare beneficiaries can review and make changes to their Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the coming year. Join HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling & Advocacy Program) for a free educational presentation covering Medicare updates taking effect in 2027, Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review strategies, and important factors to consider when evaluating your coverage options. Learn how to compare plan costs, provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and other benefits to determine whether your current plan continues to meet your needs. Following the presentation, HICAP counselors will be available for free one-on-one counseling sessions to answer Medicare questions and help attendees review their coverage options. HICAP counselors are unbiased and are not affiliated with any insurance company. The one-on-one sessions will be on a first-come, first-served basis. HICAP is a program of Sourcewise providing free Medicare counseling to Santa Clara County residents. Who Should Attend? Current Medicare beneficiaries reviewing their coverage for 2027; Individuals approaching Medicare eligibility; Family members and caregivers assisting a Medicare beneficiary. What You Will Learn: Medicare updates taking effect in 2027; How the Annual Enrollment Period works; Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review tips; How to compare costs, coverage, and provider networks; Prescription drug coverage considerations; When it may make sense to change plans; Resources and assistance available through HICAP. What to Bring: A complete list of your prescription medications, including dosage and quantity, for accurate plan comparisons. Your Medicare card (optional, but helpful). HICAP counselors will have laptops available for Medicare plan reviews, but attendees are welcome to bring their own laptop or tablet. Time Required: The time needed to complete a plan comparison varies depending on the number of prescriptions and coverage options being reviewed. Most plan reviews take approximately 30–60 minutes. This program is intended for Santa Clara County residents. Please register if you would like to receive a reminder about the presentation. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org. About Sourcewise: Since 1973, Sourcewise has provided services and support to seniors in Santa Clara County. Sourcewise aims to inform, educate, and prepare all adults within Santa Clara County to better navigate their health and life options.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep them on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Intermediate-Mass Black Holes; Meteor Showers or Space Debris?
events.description: Lecture 1: Understanding how supermassive black holes grow offers key clues to how galaxies evolve, but their "missing link"—intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs)—remains elusive. Because small, blue compact dwarf galaxies cannot host supermassive monsters, they are prime hunting grounds for IMBHs. In this talk, we explore how changes in visible gas emission lines over nearly two decades can reveal these hidden engines, highlighting recent Magellan Spectrograph observations of dwarf galaxy J1143 that point to an accreting intermediate-mass black hole at its core. Delivered by Kiera Aston. Lecture 2: Gorgeous meteor showers streaking across the zenith, or space trash entering our atmosphere? The 21st century's growing "space environment" problem is beginning to take center stage. Space debris—artificial spacecraft and objects that have ceased functioning—is accumulating in Low Earth Orbit at an unprecedented rate. We are developing a global space debris monitoring network using ground-based observations. At the core of the system is a three-channel multispectral camera designed to detect the aluminum emission line in the near-UV spectrum, providing a distinctive signature for identifying space debris as it reenters Earth's atmosphere. Delivered by Alice Zou. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear a lecture on how supermassive black holes grow and why intermediate-mass black holes remain so hard to find.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear author Dr. Carol Peyser speak at an evening author event at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Beyond the Spotlight: One Life. Multiple Passions. Endless Possibilities
events.description: In this inspiring talk with professionals, we explore how passion for the performing arts can coexist with a primary career. Can you be a professional by day and a performer by choice? What does it look like when theater becomes more than a hobby without becoming your full-time profession? Through personal stories, practical insights, and thoughtful conversation, this event invites participants to rethink traditional career paths, make space for creativity, and redefine what success can look like. We will discuss how aspiring performers can balance education, professional goals, personal responsibilities, and their love for the stage. Join us for a thought-provoking discussion on pursuing Performing Arts and Theater as a Parallel Career Path: an exploration of passion, purpose, possibility, and the courage to embrace more than one professional identity. Carla Pantoja: Carla, born and raised in the South Bay, is an actor, fight director, teaching artist, intimacy director, and mom of two. She has been a Resident Artist of San Francisco Shakespeare Festival since 2014 and recently served as Director of Vision for the 2021 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Pericles, Prince of Tyre, directing episodes 2 and 4. In 2020, she was in the acting company at Oregon Shakespeare Festival, returning in 2022 as the festival's first female fight director. Carla is an associate instructor for Dueling Arts International and serves on their governing body as President. She is also a proud member of Making Good Trouble, an anti-racist training cohort based in the Bay Area. Carla has directed SF Shakes' Shakespeare on Tour productions of Romeo and Juliet and Comedy of Errors and assistant-directed the 2017 Free Shakespeare in the Park production of Hamlet. She played Paulina in Free Shakespeare in the Park's The Winter's Tale, Tybalt in Romeo and Juliet, and Kate in The Taming of the Shrew. She's performed with Cal Shakes, Shotgun Players, Crowded Fire, Playground, Lorraine Hansberry Theatre, and the SF Mime Troupe in the Bay Area, to name a few. Vinay Pande: Vinay Pande is a Silicon Valley technology leader and a passionate theatre artist who brings together the worlds of innovation and performing arts. Originally from Mumbai, India, Vinay holds a degree in Instrumentation Engineering and began his career in telecommunications, where he was part of the core team that developed India's first satellite-based mission-critical voice, data, and video network for the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). He later worked as a researcher at the prestigious Bell Labs, holds 15 technology patents, and has co-authored technical publications and books. Today, he serves as a Principal Architect at a leading technology company in Silicon Valley. Beyond his technology career, Vinay has nurtured a deep passion for the performing arts for over a decade, actively pursuing theatre, acting, and singing across Marathi and Hindi productions. From bringing diverse characters to life on stage to engaging audiences as a Radio Jockey and event host, he thrives on the energy of live performance and the magic of storytelling. For Vinay, technology may be his profession, but the stage is where his creative spirit truly comes alive. Sowmya Renukuntla: Sowmya is a Bay Area native and recent graduate from Santa Clara University, where she studied Business and worked directly with Admission Counselors for four years. Since graduating, she has been working full-time at Levi Strauss & Co. on the Corporate Insights team and is a part-time college counselor. Sponsored by the Cupertino Library Foundation. events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes.
events.blurb: Draw with pencils in timed rounds of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute, in a one-hour figure-drawing workshop.

events.description: The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) are hosting a friendly needlework stitch-in. Come join us from 10 am to 2 pm in the conference room; there are always extra seats! The South Bay Needlepointers (SBN) chapter of the American Needlepoint Guild was chartered on March 1, 1986. We meet monthly at the Milpitas Police Department Community Room. At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint. The purpose of the American Needlepoint Guild is for education and cultural development through participation in and encouragement of interest in the art of needlepoint, which is defined as needlework executed by hand with a threaded needle on a readily counted ground. If you would like to find out more about SBN, please join us at one of our meetings or contact us at: sbnangcontact@gmail.com.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: We'll be reading Elatsoe by Darcie Little Badger in honor of Native American Heritage Month. Sign up at the adult reference desk to get a copy. "Imagine an America very similar to our own. It's got homework, best friends, and pistachio ice cream. There are some differences. This America has been shaped dramatically by the magic, monsters, knowledge, and legends of its peoples, those Indigenous and those not. Some of these forces are charmingly everyday, like the ability to make an orb of light appear or travel across the world through rings of fungi. But other forces are less charming and should never see the light of day. Seventeen-year-old Elatsoe ("Ellie" for short) lives in this slightly stranger America. She can raise the ghosts of dead animals, a skill passed down through generations of her Lipan Apache family. Her beloved cousin has just been murdered, in a town that wants no prying eyes. But she is going to do more than pry. The picture-perfect façade of Willowbee masks gruesome secrets, and she will rely on her wits, skills, and friends to tear off the mask and protect her family." events.title: AI Scam and Fraud - A Community Conversation
events.description: Artificial Intelligence is reshaping how we work and connect with each other - but what does that actually mean for our everyday lives, and what future are we heading towards? Join us as we discuss a specific part of AI that is currently all over the news: AI-enabled scams and fraud. This is a free and open event - we'll watch a video and learn together, then discuss our opinions. You'll come away with a better understanding of AI and develop your own ideas about this transformational technology. How is AI enabling scams and fraud? What are the larger ramifications of this harm? Come join your neighbors for a discussion and think through what a good AI future looks like for our community. The Los Altos Library has proudly partnered with the AI Safety Awareness Project to host and run this discussion. events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never-before-seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film, including KQED, but national PBS has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers. Registration is not required, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن، به ما بپیوندید. در این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Photography Meetup
events.description: Join us for a monthly meetup designed for intermediate and advanced photographers hosted by Matthew Tw Huang. Whether you're into portrait, landscape, or any other type of photography, all are welcome! Each session will feature discussions on techniques, tips for improving your craft, and other aspects of photography. Ideas for 5-10 min topics, photo stories, or presentations can be emailed to matthewtwhuang@gmail.com. There will be time for a couple of ideas to be presented at each meeting. The format will evolve based on your interests and feedback, creating a supportive and dynamic space for photographers to connect, learn, and grow.
events.blurb: Discuss techniques and swap tips with fellow intermediate and advanced photographers at this monthly meetup led by Matthew Tw Huang.

events.title: Tai Chi with Nelson Ng
events.description: Join us for Tai Chi sessions with Nelson Ng! In this weekly class, participants will learn the basic principles and the philosophy behind Tai Chi, gaining flexibility and a better sense of balance through slow, gentle movement. Nelson started learning Chen's Tai Chi in 1989 from Master Gene Chen, who was a disciple of Grandmaster Feng Zhi Qiang. Nelson has been teaching since 2014. This class is free and open to beginners as well as those who have previous Tai Chi experience. People of all ages are welcome. You must sign in upon arrival.
events.blurb: Learn Tai Chi principles and practice slow, gentle movements with instructor Nelson Ng to build balance and flexibility.

events.title: Vintage Media Lab
events.description: Preserve your old photographs, home movies, records and cassettes! How to Access: Check the Vintage Media Lab page. Each appointment includes a skilled volunteer or staff person to assist you. Appointments are limited to a single two-hour appointment per week per person. Because space and time in the Vintage Media Lab are limited, we appreciate your cooperation in regard to equipment, storage and cleanliness. What to Bring: Laptop; SD Card, Memory Card; USB Drive, Flash Drive or Memory Stick; External Hard Drive; Your Vintage Media!

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line with Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Here's a chance to talk to a writer about his writing process and to hear how he came to write this novel. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Talk with local author Raj Oza about Double Play on the Red Line and hear how he came to write the novel.

events.title: Open Sewing Studio
events.description: Do you have a sewing project but need the equipment and space? Are you interested in learning about the basics of a sewing machine? Open Sewing Studio is a space for both beginners looking to learn as well as experienced sewists looking for the time and space to work on their project. We will have sewing machines, table space, fabric scraps, and tools available for attendees. Bring your own projects and have fun! Note: Teens and adults only. Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply. Our staff is only available to support very basic projects. Please keep in mind Open Sewing Studio is limited to 1.5 hours.
events.attendanceNote: Use of machines will be on a first-come, first-served basis due to limited supply.
events.blurb: Bring your sewing project and use the library's machines and space, or learn the basics as a beginner.

Staff is available to help with a variety of tech questions including: Learning to use Libby and/or Hoopla; Accessing library databases and services; Downloading and streaming content; Navigating the City of Palo Alto Library website; Downloading and using the new PACL app; Wi-Fi connection; Printing; Creating an email account; Basic computer skills; Installing and using common apps; And more… Unfortunately, helping you fix damaged hardware or software is not within our scope. Help is given on a first-come, first-served basis. Please bring any devices you use, make sure they are charged, and have your necessary passwords. We look forward to helping you.
events.attendanceNote: Help is given on a first-come, first-served basis. Please bring any devices you use, make sure they are charged, and have your necessary passwords. We look forward to helping you.
events.blurb: Bring your technology questions or ongoing device problems to Rinconada Library for drop-in help on Tuesday mornings.

events.title: Bilingual Family Storytime
events.description: Join Señorita Juliana for Bilingual Family Storytime at the College Terrace Library! Enjoy stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities in Spanish and English. Thursdays from 10:30-11 AM. Storytime may be held indoors or outdoors depending on the weather. Follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs, and rhymes, including a playlist of our favorites! ¡Participa con la Señorita Juliana en la Hora de Cuentos Bilingüe en la Biblioteca College Terrace! Disfruta de cuentos, canciones, rimas y actividades con movimiento en español e inglés. Jueves de 10:30-11 AM. La Hora de Cuentos se realizará adentro o al aire libre, dependiendo del clima. ¡Síguenos en YouTube para ver más cuentos, canciones y rimas, incluyendo una lista de reproducción con nuestros favoritos!
events.blurb: Sing songs and rhymes, and join in movement activities in Spanish and English with Señorita Juliana at Bilingual Family Storytime.

events.title: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Sit for guided sitting and releasing meditation with Phuong Pham, then join a group sharing and Q&A session.

events.title: Big Bunny 5K and Kids Fun Run
events.address: Cupertino Civic Center, 10300 Torre Avenue, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Lace up and join the fun at the Big Bunny 5K! Run, walk, or hop your way through a 3.1-mile course winding through the streets of Cupertino, starting and finishing at the Cupertino Civic Center. Whether you're racing for a personal best or enjoying a morning out with friends and family, this community fun run is the perfect way to kick off the day. For our youngest participants (ages 7 and under), we offer a special kid-friendly course on Library Field—short, sweet, and designed for maximum fun. Everyone who participates is a winner!
events.blurb: Run, walk, or hop a 3.1-mile course through Cupertino streets, starting and finishing at the Civic Center, with a kids fun run too.

events.title: Who Wears This Hat? with Rochelle Rabouin
events.description: Listen to stories about hats and learn about the many service occupations and situations where people traditionally wear hats. Participants will discover how these "hat wearing people" benefit our local and global community. We strongly encourage you to wear a hat! About the presenter: Rochelle Rabouin is a vocalist, musician, master teaching artist, arts in education-enrichment specialist, consultant, trainer and author. She creates and presents education-based programs that are also fun.
events.blurb: Listen to stories about hats and the service jobs where people wear them, with storyteller Rochelle Rabouin; wearing a hat is encouraged.

events.title: Math Club
events.description: Improve your math skills and apply them through fun math-related activities! Participants will focus on a variety of math concepts and do hands-on math activities in this weekly drop-in program. For children in grades 3-5 only. Registration not required. Instruction on the week's concept will occur during the first 15-20 minutes, so please arrive on time. This program meets in person during the school year. We may cancel some meetings due to school/holiday breaks or volunteer unavailability.
events.blurb: Tackle hands-on math activities and concepts each week in this drop-in club for grades 3-5.

events.title: 3D Printeen
events.description: We're holding an introduction to 3D printing class for teens. If you are curious about 3D printing and would like to learn more about how to find or design a 3D model, then join us for this fun program. All teens are invited to join. We will create a 3D model, then run it through a 3D slicer program, then watch the printer make the model in real-time. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Library and the San José Public Library Foundation's Pat Dando Endowment.
events.blurb: Learn how to find or design a 3D model in an introductory 3D printing class for teens.

events.description: Are you a student in grades K-6 who needs help with homework? Trained tutors offer free homework help every Tuesday and Thursday from 4:30 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. No registration is required. Basic school supplies will be provided. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

events.title: Leyendo en español para niños - Reading to Children in Spanish
events.description: Nuestra voluntaria maravillosa leerá cuentos en inglés y español para niños y sus familias. La participación en este programa es una manera excelente para que los niños desarrollen su imaginación y despierten el amor por los libros. Our wonderful volunteer will read stories in both English and Spanish to children and their families. Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning.
events.blurb: Bring the kids to hear a volunteer read stories aloud in both English and Spanish.

events.title: Fiber Arts Circle
events.description: Do you enjoy crocheting or knitting? Want to see what others are working on, refine your skills, or connect with other crafters? Grab your project and join us every week in the Almaden Library living room (behind the Tech Center where the newspapers and magazines are kept) to crochet or knit (or embroider or tat or...) and chat with other crafters making things with yarn. All hand needle crafts welcome. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library.
events.blurb: Bring your crochet or knitting project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the library's living room.

events.title: Earth and Arbor Day Festival
events.description: Cupertino's annual Earth and Arbor Day Festival is an interactive event that invites community members of all ages to learn about environmental issues and solutions in a family-friendly atmosphere. Explore booths, hands-on activities, live entertainment, and food trucks. Connect with local organizations working to protect our environment at this free community event. For additional information on the City's Earth and Arbor Day festival, see the Earth and Arbor Day Festival webpage.
events.blurb: Learn about environmental issues and solutions at Cupertino's annual festival, with interactive activities for all ages.

events.title: Stanford Blood Drive
events.description: Give Blood and Save Lives! The Milpitas Library is hosting the Stanford Blood Center Blood Drive. Schedule an appointment using the QR code below. For more information, email Aprille Walsh at aprillew@stanford.edu. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Give blood at the Stanford Blood Center drive hosted in the Milpitas Library, using the posted QR code to schedule an appointment.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Free. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Sing songs, trade rhymes, and move along with early literacy activities built for families with kids of mixed ages.

events.title: Monthly STEM Workshop
events.description: Join us for our monthly STEM Workshop presented by teen volunteers in Girls Empowered in Math and Science (GEMS)! This one-hour workshop includes a brief presentation explaining the concepts involved in the activities. Each month has a different theme! Free. No registration required. Recommended for elementary school students. Presented by teen volunteers in Girls Empowered in Math and Science (GEMS). Special thanks to the Friends of the Cambrian Library for their generosity!
events.blurb: Join a one-hour hands-on STEM workshop led by teen GEMS volunteers, with a short presentation explaining the concepts behind each month's themed activities.

events.title: Monday Matinee: Smoke Signals
events.description: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month with the 1998 film Smoke Signals. Smoke Signals--one of the first feature films to be written, directed, and produced by Native Americans--won the Audience Award at Sundance. The film follows Victor Joseph and Thomas Builds-the-Fire, who travel from their Idaho reservation to collect the ashes of Victor's estranged father. Rated PG-13; 89 minutes. Movie trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vQhviwp8j38. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Watch the 1998 film Smoke Signals, a Sundance Audience Award winner written, directed, and produced by Native Americans, for Native American Heritage Month.

events.description: Join us for a watercolor workshop for adults. All supplies will be provided. Registration is not necessary. Seating will be determined on a first-come, first-served basis. events.title: A Look into the Night Sky with Astro Everywhere
events.description: Join us at the Children's Library for a special evening of astronomy with Astro Everywhere! We'll gather in the Treetop Room for a live astronomy show featuring planetarium software to explore the night sky as seen from Palo Alto. Then, head to the Secret Garden for a telescope demonstration and a closer look at the Moon and Saturn. We'll wrap up the evening with a cozy cup of hot cocoa! Thank you to the Friends of the Palo Alto Library (FOPAL) for their generous support.
events.blurb: Watch a live astronomy show in the Treetop Room, using planetarium software to see the night sky as it appears over Palo Alto.

events.title: Tutoring Kidz
events.description: Join us for a fun and exciting tutoring program led by two high school students, Addison and Sarah! Their goal is to make learning an enjoyable and rewarding experience for every student. Through engaging games, creative activities, and interactive lessons, they help students strengthen their English and math skills while building confidence and discovering the joy of learning. Come learn, play, and succeed! Perfect for children ages 5–12! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Work through tutoring sessions led by two high school students, Addison and Sarah, who aim to make learning enjoyable.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Get ready to build, create, and let your imagination soar at LEGO Club! With LEGO and Duplo bricks, families can drop in and bring their wildest ideas to life. Whether you're constructing towers, spaceships, or entire worlds, the possibilities are endless. Make lasting memories every Saturday and leave feeling like everything is awesome! Note: Recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop in with the family and build towers, spaceships, and whatever else you imagine with LEGO and Duplo bricks.

events.title: Teen Resource Fair
events.address: Main Street Cupertino, 19401 Stevens Creek Boulevard, 95014
events.description: This event is focused on helping teens explore City of Cupertino summer job opportunities and volunteer programs that build real-world skills and look great on college and job applications. Learn about opportunities like REV, YAB, LIT, and Techie Teens, and meet the staff who coordinate and recruit for these programs. In addition, the fair will include mental health and wellness resources through IDC Wellness, so teens can also learn what support is available to them.
events.blurb: Meet City of Cupertino staff and learn about summer job and volunteer opportunities for teens at this resource fair.

Each month, discover a new video game, world and experience as you share insights, thoughts and tips with others! Games of the month (titles subject to change at staff discretion): November - Castlevania; December - The Legend of Zelda.

events.description: The men in black are back! Here are links to a few videos from Nathan's YouTube channel to put you in the mood: The Vision by Rob Reich, May 2025; Comes Love, October 2022; House of the Rising Sun, December 2024. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Community Threads: Lunar New Year Felt Goat
events.description: It's the year of the goat! In this workshop, folks will make a felt goat for Lunar New Year. We will only be hand sewing in this workshop. Open to teens and adults only. The workshop is suitable for the advanced beginner, intermediate, or advanced sewist. Knowledge of hand sewing and the sewing machine is required. You should know how to thread the machine, fill the bobbin, and use the backstitch, and you should understand the various other parts and functions of the sewing machine.
events.blurb: Hand-sew a felt goat for Lunar New Year in this teen and adult workshop at Mitchell Park Library.

events.title: LEGO Fun!
events.description: Lots and lots of LEGOs... Seriously, a lot. This program is held every third Sunday of the month at Bascom. Create something cool? We can display a photo of it on the library's LCD TV! Ask staff and we'll take a photo of it. For children and families. Registration recommended but not required. Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards. LEGO by Alexander Lowe; Amazing Vehicles by Rona Skene
events.attendanceNote: Registration is recommended but not required.
events.blurb: Build with a huge pile of LEGO bricks and maybe get your creation displayed on the library TV.

events.title: Music & Movement
events.description: Bring your dancing feet to the Mitchell Park Library on Wednesday evenings for Music & Movement with Librarian Celina. Build early literacy skills through movement, songs, and dance. This week, we'll be celebrating Native American Heritage Month. Instruments, songs, and dance moves will all be introduced so that everyone will be able to enjoy moving along to the music. This program is meant for families with children, and no previous experience is needed!
events.blurb: Dance, sing, and play instruments with Librarian Celina in a Native American Heritage Month celebration.

events.title: Indian Classical Dance Program
events.description: Saratoga Library presents classical dances from India by accomplished Bay Area classical dancers. 12:50 PM - Innovation Song by Nivedha Balan; 1:00 PM - 1:45 PM: Kathak Dance by Vyoma Bhanap; 2:00 PM - 2:45 PM: Kuchipudi Dance by Jaanya Annapureddy; 3:00 PM - 3:45 PM: Bharatanatyam Dance by Smt. Aishwarya Venkat; 4:00 PM - 4:45 PM: Bharatnatyam Dance by Vatsal Dave. All are welcome. Thanks to Friends of the Saratoga Libraries for sponsoring the program.
events.blurb: Watch accomplished Bay Area classical dancers perform dances from India at Saratoga Library on Saturday afternoon.

events.title: Chess Club
events.description: Join us to learn and play one of the world's oldest board games! Kids and teens interested in chess are welcome to our Chess Club to play with other chess enthusiasts and sharpen their skills! This is the place to find a partner to play with and learn together. Our volunteers, who are high school chess club members, will play with the kids and provide commentary and advice on the games. Chess sets and boards are provided. Free. Registration required.
events.blurb: Play chess with other kids and teens, find a partner, and sharpen your skills while learning alongside fellow players on Saturday afternoon.

This program is primarily for children age 1-5 and their parents/caregivers, but youth of all ages are welcome. Free, with limited capacity.
