events.description: A monthly discussion of the best in mystery fiction. Please join us on the first Wednesday of each month at 10:15 am. This month's book is The Frozen River, by Ariel Lawhon. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Join a discussion of Ariel Lawhon's The Frozen River with fellow mystery readers at the monthly Whodunit? book club.

events.title: OneInMath: Math Program for K-3
events.description: Join us for a free math program for students in kindergarten through 3rd grade to learn basic arithmetic, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division using one- to four-digit numbers. It is taught by trained high school students. The focus is to build confidence and a love for math in young students. For registration information, please visit oneinmath.com. This program is suitable for children in grades K-3. Free. Registration required.
events.blurb: Practice addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division in a free math program for kindergarten through 3rd grade, taught by trained high school students.

events.title: English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: This program is held in person at Educational Park Branch Library. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Look no further! Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English-speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome!
events.blurb: Practice your spoken English with other learners in a welcoming, low-pressure conversation club.

events.title: Friends of the Campbell Library Used Book Sale
events.description: Join us for the Friends of the Campbell Library used book sale! Items for sale include puzzles, games, hardback fiction books, children's books, romances, thrillers, audio books, DVDs, CDs, and a variety of 'how to' books. Pay cash, check, Zelle, card, or Venmo. Remember to bring a bag for your purchases! Sign up to hear about more upcoming Book Sales at the Friends of the Campbell Library's website: Sales - Friends of the Campbell Library
events.blurb: Browse used puzzles, books, DVDs, and CDs at the Friends of the Campbell Library book sale.

events.title: Sunday CrafterNoon
events.description: All-ages arts and crafts! Adults, teens, and kids -- join us for an afternoon of relaxed crafting on the third Sunday of the month. Supplies are provided for you to explore a surprise art activity. This craft is self-directed; children must come with their responsible adult crafting-buddy. The room closes at 3:30 PM, so please give yourself enough time to finish your craft. If you like, you are welcome to complete it at home.
events.blurb: Drop in with your kids and craft a surprise art project together during this relaxed all-ages afternoon session.

events.title: Children's Bingo
events.description: Come play Bingo and win cool prizes! Join us Monday, November 23rd at 4 PM in Room 101. For school-age children. Generously sponsored by the Friends of Cupertino Library! For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Play bingo for prizes in Room 101, with school-age children welcome and the event sponsored by the Friends of Cupertino Library.

events.title: Clases de inglés para hispanos - Nivel 1
events.description: ¿Quieres mejorar tu vocabulario en inglés, aprender gramática y hacer amigos? Te invitamos a participar en esta clase de inglés de nivel 1, dirigida por el voluntario Mike. Esta clase es solo para personas cuyo primer idioma es el español. No habrá clases los días 11 y 25 de noviembre de 2026. events.blurb: Practice English vocabulary and grammar with volunteer instructor Mike in this Spanish-speakers' beginner class.

events.description: Join the Bay Area Quiz Club for fun trivia and friendly competition! Bay Area Quiz Club (BAQC) is a volunteer-run organization. Our quizzes take place from 2-6 PM on the second Sunday of every month, at Mitchell Park Library, Palo Alto. It is free and open to everyone.

events.description: Make your own mini masterpieces at the library! Get to know other teens in your community and let your creative juices flow as you paint your own mini canvas. This program is for teens ages 13-18. While supplies last. One canvas per teen. All materials will be provided, but you're welcome to bring your own supplies. Free. No registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Santa Teresa Branch.
events.blurb: Paint your own mini canvas and meet other teens at this library craft session for ages 13 to 18.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) for Beginners / Inglés Para Principiantes (ELL)
events.description: English Language Learners are invited to beginner-friendly lessons at the Rose Garden Branch Library. Lessons will be taught by an experienced ELL teacher. Free. No registration required. Invitamos a las personas interesadas en aprender inglés a participar en nuestras clases para principiantes en la Biblioteca Rose Garden. Las lecciones serán impartidas por un docente experimentado de ELL. Gratis. No es necesario registrarse.
events.blurb: Practice English in beginner-friendly lessons taught by an experienced ELL teacher, free with no registration required.

events.title: Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: Need tech assistance? Drop by for personalized support at our Tech Drop-Ins. Whether it's software updates, data transfers, or general computer queries, our experts are here to help. Explore affordable internet options, navigate ACP transitions, and discover a wealth of technology resources. Let's tackle your tech challenges together. Tech help available in English and Vietnamese. Hỗ trợ có sẵn bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt.
events.blurb: Drop in for personalized tech help with software updates, data transfers, internet options, and general computer questions.

events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Wednesday mornings at 10:30 AM for Little Ones Storytime at Children's Library. Storytime includes a variety of early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is targeted to children under the age of two and their caregivers.
events.blurb: Bring little ones to sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi on Wednesday mornings.

events.title: Mastering Your Cellphone
events.description: Technology moves very fast and sometimes it can feel overwhelming! Don't worry - San Jose Public Library is here to help! Seniors who have Apple or Android cellphones are welcome to come to our free presentation that will teach you the basics of how to use your device: how to install apps, how to take photos, how to message friends and family, and how to be safe while using your phone! Users of all skill levels are welcome!
events.blurb: Get help with your cellphone from San Jose Public Library, in a session for anyone who finds fast-changing technology overwhelming.

events.title: Cupertino Spelling Bee
events.address: Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is an annual contest for Cupertino students in grades 2-5, and is organized by the Cupertino Parks and Recreation Department and the Cupertino Youth Activity Board. Please note: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is not affiliated with the National Scripps Spelling Bee and we cannot sponsor or send winners to the National Spelling Bee. Registration will open with winter activity registration.
events.blurb: Watch Cupertino students in grades 2 to 5 compete in the annual spelling bee run by Parks and Recreation and the Youth Activity Board.

events.title: Bilingual Family Storytime
events.description: This 30-minute storytime features movement, singing, and action! The early literacy focus is on sharing stories and songs in English and Mandarin Chinese. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Sing, move, and hear stories in English and Mandarin during this 30-minute evening storytime.

events.title: Community Threads: Holiday Placemat
events.description: In this workshop, folks will learn how to make a festive holiday placemat to decorate their homes for the holidays. The workshop is suitable for the advanced beginner, intermediate, or advanced sewist. Knowledge of the sewing machine is required. You should know how to thread the machine, fill the bobbin, and use the backstitch, and you should understand the various other parts and functions of the sewing machine. Open to teens and adults only.
events.blurb: Sew a festive holiday placemat in this workshop for advanced beginner to advanced sewists.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our reading volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud with our volunteer. Please note: this is not a tutoring session. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Meet a reading volunteer for one-on-one or small group storytime and practice reading aloud yourself.

events.title: Art of Living Meditation
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Why wait to find greater peace in your life? Join volunteers from the Art of Living Foundation every Sat. morning at 11:00 AM for a relaxing meditation session. Sessions will include simple yoga stretches that can be done sitting on a chair, calming breathing techniques (pranayama), and a guided meditation. Art of Living volunteers will be available after the meditation to answer questions. Beginners are welcome.
events.blurb: Join Art of Living Foundation volunteers for a Saturday morning meditation session at the library.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.
events.blurb: Play modern board games at Downtown Library, bringing your own or joining a table with other gamers during the day-long meetup.

events.title: Ukraine: Culture, Geography, History and Heritage
events.description: Nora Mason, a native-born Ukrainian and long-time Saratoga resident, will present a program on the culture of Ukraine and how its geography has contributed to tragic invasions over time. She will share her family's WWII story and how they ultimately immigrated to the United States. She will also touch on inspiring efforts to help the people of Ukraine today. Program co-sponsored by the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW.
events.blurb: Hear Ukrainian-born Saratoga resident Nora Mason talk about Ukraine's culture and how its geography has shaped its history of invasions.

events.title: Tech Mentor
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Need help printing or using Word and Excel? Want to set up an email account? Need ideas on tech security? Questions about accessing SJPL e-resources? From the basics to somewhat beyond, volunteer tech mentors are here to help with thoughtful advice and problem-solving. We will do our best to assist you with your tech dilemmas. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Bring your questions on printing, Word, Excel, email setup, or tech security to volunteer tech mentors who offer advice and problem-solving.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: Whether you're picking up a hook for the first time or you're a seasoned pro, come stitch with us! Work on your own project, start something new, or learn the basics with help from our knowledgeable volunteer. It's a relaxed, creative space to build skills and connect with fellow crochet lovers of all ages. Hooks, yarn, and basic supplies provided while supplies last. Ages 8 and up. All skill levels welcome.
events.blurb: Bring your own crochet project or learn the basics from a volunteer in a relaxed stitching circle.

events.title: LEGO Spike Robots!
events.description: Learn basic engineering and coding while having LEGO-style fun with LEGO Spike Prime! Participants will follow simple step-by-step picture instructions on a tablet to build an exciting frog, dog, or other kind of robot, and then learn to use simple Word Blocks to make their robot perform their commands! This program is great for beginners. No prior experience is necessary. Limited to 10 participants. Free.
events.blurb: Build and code LEGO Spike Prime robots while picking up basic engineering skills at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Neighborhood Hands Bi-monthly Cleanup
events.description: Our pilot program meets every other Saturday at 7:45 a.m. in Guadalupe Gardens just north of the Spring St. cul-de-sac off Coleman Avenue across from Target. (Google Maps directions here; see red pin on map below.) If the weather is good, we clean the park until approximately 9:15 a.m.; unhoused neighbors receive stipends, and then everyone enjoys a vibrant and growing community resource fair until ~10:30 a.m.
events.blurb: Help clean Guadalupe Gardens, then stay for the community resource fair.

events.description: Pick up a checklist at the table in the Children's Area. Look for the images around the Children's Area. Once you have found all of the images on the checklist, come to the table in the Children's Area for a prize (while supplies last!) Themes vary each week. Free. No registration required. While supplies last. This will take place in the Children's Area from 1 PM-2 PM. No scavenger hunt on 11/07/2026.
events.blurb: Grab a checklist and hunt for hidden images around the Children's Area to win a small prize.

events.title: Pottery for Kids
events.description: Make your own pot with air-dry clay in the style of traditional Istalif pottery while learning about girls' access to education in Afghanistan. This is a free, youth-led program. All materials will be provided. Attendance is limited. Participants must pick up a ticket at the Information Desk. Tickets will be available 1 hour prior to the program's start time. Child must be present to receive a ticket.

events.description: ¿Quieres mejorar tu vocabulario en inglés, aprender gramática y hacer amigos? Te invitamos a participar en esta clase de inglés nivel cero dirigida por la voluntaria Christin. Esta clase es solamente para personas cuyo primer idioma es el español. ¡Inscríbete ahora! ¡El espacio es limitado! Gratis. Se proporcionará el material educativo. Para mayor información, escribe a marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Practice English vocabulary and grammar in a class led by a volunteer, open to people whose first language is Spanish.

events.title: Make Your Own Pop Art
events.description: Join us to create your own pop art image. We will be using iPads, Apple Pencils, the Sketchbook app and Keynote. Explore different features across these apps to learn the fundamentals of photo editing. Transforming ordinary objects, such as figurines and erasers, allows participants to find artistic and scientific beauty in the world around them. Recommended for ages 8 and up. No experience required.
events.blurb: Make your own pop art image using iPads, Apple Pencils, the Sketchbook app and Keynote while learning photo editing fundamentals.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One-on-One Computer Help
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as printing, using email, connecting to Wi-Fi, creating documents, and accessing library resources such as e-books. We can also provide basic instructions for using devices such as laptops, smartphones, e-readers, etc. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.
events.blurb: Get personalized help with email, printing, Wi-Fi, and more at this Monday tech session.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club: Beginning
events.description: Come practice English with us! Learners will study everyday vocabulary and basic listening and speaking skills. Suitable for beginning English learners. Free. events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an exhibit
events.description: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments played in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down through generations, which are still played around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit, which starts on November 14, 2026, and closes on December 5, 2026. The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv

events.title: Volunteer in the Historic Orchard with UC Master Gardeners!
events.description: The Historic Orchard is a 3.3-acre site planted in 1994 and located in Guadalupe Gardens just south of Taylor Street, adjacent to the Heritage Rose Garden and River Park trails. In the 1930s and '40s, almost everyone who lived here was engaged in the business of fruit production: growing, picking, packing, canning, selling, or otherwise supporting the industry. Today, with very few orchards remaining, this is a place where adults and children can come to experience a piece of local history. Fruit harvested from the Historic Orchard is donated to Second Harvest of Silicon Valley and local shelters. Help us maintain the River Park's Historic Orchard with activities including tree planting and pruning; disease diagnosis and treatment; sun scald prevention painting; sheet mulching; experimenting with different types of irrigation or ground cover; and grafting for improved pollination. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Restrooms are available at the Rotary Play Garden and will require staff assistance. Address for parking: 438 Coleman Ave. Jose, CA 95110; Meeting location: Historic Orchard (refer to the registration form for a map); Time: 9:30 AM - 11:30 AM; Recurring dates: Every Wednesday
events.attendanceNote: Advance registration is required through Guadalupe River Park Conservancy. Meet at Historic Orchard; see the organizer's registration form for the meeting map. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!); Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with the community at Mitchell Park Community Center's Festival of Lights.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music; no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Location Change: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for a mindfulness meditation session at the Art Center Meeting Room.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Night Hike and Flashlight Tour
events.description: Enjoy a fun-filled Night Hike and Flashlight Tour of McClellan Ranch Preserve and Blackberry Farm! We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.attendanceNote: All attendees must register. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
events.blurb: Walk McClellan Ranch Preserve after dark with a ranger, learning how nocturnal animals adapt to nighttime.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.

events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

events.title: Jane! An intimate exploration of Gilded Age excess and the enigmatic life and death of Jane Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Museum hours: Mon & Fri: 11 AM–6 PM; Thurs: 11 AM–8 PM; Sat & Sun: 10 AM–5 PM. Closed: Tues and Wed.
events.description: Curated by Associate Curator of European Art Patrick R. Crowley, Jane! celebrates the aesthetic and affective excesses of Jane Stanford, the Gilded Age founder and matriarch of Stanford University.
events.blurb: Tour the Cantor Arts Center exhibit on Jane Stanford's Gilded Age excess and mysterious death.

events.title: Electric Contrasts: the Art of the Detail
events.description: Electric Contrasts: The Art of the Detail brings together photobooks and magazines to show how the revolution of photography in the late 19th and early 20th centuries changed the history of art.
events.attendanceNote: Visitors are asked to call 650-723-3408 for building and elevator access to Bowes Art & Architecture Library.
events.blurb: Browse photobooks and magazines tracing how early photography reshaped art history at the McMurtry Building.

events.title: Korean Indigenous Futures: The Art of Kim Bong-Jun
events.description: The East Asia Library at Stanford University will host a print exhibition by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung (People's) Art, from September 29 to December 11, 2026.
events.blurb: View prints by Kim Bong-Jun, a leading figure in Korean Minjung People's Art, at Lathrop Library.

events.title: Emergent Properties: Decennial Reflections on Collections
events.description: In 2026 the David Rumsey Map Center celebrates its tenth year—a moment to reflect on how the Center has added value to scholarship on campus and around the world.
events.blurb: Browse the David Rumsey Map Center's decennial exhibit reflecting on ten years of its collections.

events.title: Patty Chang: surfacing
events.description: In surfacing, Patty Chang engages the ocean as a physical, geopolitical, and symbolic space, inviting you to consider the work of collection and recollection.
events.blurb: See Patty Chang's surfacing, an exhibit treating the ocean as a physical, geopolitical and symbolic space tied to collection and recollection.

events.title: Green Library Book Display: Witches and Witchcraft
events.description: Green Library's latest book display features books on "Witches and Witchcraft."
events.blurb: Browse Green Library's book display on witches and witchcraft at Hohbach Hall, open as an ongoing exhibit.

events.title: Branner Library Book & Map Exhibit - Water in the West
events.attendanceNote: Visitors must present a valid, physical government-issued photo ID and sign in at the front desk.
events.blurb: Browse Branner Library's book and map exhibit on water history in the American West.

events.title: Text Machines: Scarlet Thread of the Digital Order (1883-2026)
events.blurb: Browse the Text Machines exhibit on digital order at Green Library's Bing Wing.

events.title: A Vision of Paris: The Roxane Debuisson Collection at Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Bring a valid government ID and register at the entrance to Green Library to view the exhibition.
events.blurb: View the Roxane Debuisson Collection's vision of Paris at Green Library's Bing Wing.
